description: Step 6, close-out. One pass confirming the constructor table (list/map/tuple/resource/scalars) is accurate post-fold; DOCUMENT explicitly that tuple/tuple(T,U) named forms are intentionally NOT added ({T,U} stays sole syntax) unless reviewer wants that parity (open question, don't build speculatively). Update .agent/docs type-resolution section to name the registry as the single source of truth (present-tense per docs convention). Depends fz-usm.1-.4 (and .5's decision).

comments.text:
Parity audit complete for the resolve.rs CONSTRUCTORS registry (the table this
ticket names): all 13 nullary scalars + list/resource (parametric) + map are
present, each already had test coverage proving it mints the identical Ty a
direct Types call produces (resolve_test.rs). Added two new pinning tests
(bare_tuple_is_not_a_registered_constructor_name,
applied_tuple_is_not_a_registered_constructor_name) documenting that `tuple`/
`tuple(T,U)` are deliberately absent -- {T,U} stays the sole tuple syntax --
so a future registry edit can't reintroduce that gap un-reviewed. Updated the
CONSTRUCTORS doc comment in resolve.rs with the same rationale, and expanded
.agent/docs/type-naming.md with a new "Builtin constructors are one registry"
section naming resolve.rs's CONSTRUCTORS as the single source of truth for
builtin type-constructor names, including the list/[T] and map/%{} structural
concordance and the tuple-absence decision.

Adjacent finding surfaced during the audit (not in this ticket's scope, filed
separately per no-silent-deferrals): the registry this ticket closes out is
the sole authority for *type-annotation* name resolution
(resolve.rs::classify_name), but two OTHER independent name->Ty sites still
exist and were never reconciled against it:
- fz-usm.7: source_publish.rs's collect_type_refs (the reference-walk/publish
  side) never consults CONSTRUCTORS, only reference_type -- a user @type that
  shadows a builtin name (e.g. `@type list :: ...`) gets a real TypeDefined
  reference recorded at publish time, then silently ignored at resolve time
  because classify_name checks find_constructor first. Latent bug, not
  authorized to fix here.
- fz-usm.8: world.rs's BuiltinValueFamily (defimpl target dispatch, ~line
  3190-3247) is a second hand-maintained name->Ty table, keyed by capitalized
  module name (List/Map/...) rather than lowercase type-position name, and
  missing a Tuple family (defimpl ..., for: Tuple falls through to Nominal).
  Whether this should fold into CONSTRUCTORS or stay separate (different
  domain: protocol-impl-target names vs. type-annotation names) is an open
  design question, not decided here.

Verify: cargo test --lib -- 1296 passed, 0 failed (16 in
compiler2::resolve_test, up from 14). cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D
warnings clean.

title: fz-usm: parity audit across the constructor set + update type-resolution agent docs to name the registry as source of truth
